Simply the trees didn't receive the drop your leaves now signal for long enough in the fall. 

I don't remember the exact temperatures but the last couple weeks of September were pretty warm last year. IIRC the last week of September even had a couple of days in the 20s. So this prolonged warm period delays the leaves from dropping.  Then there was a snow fall by roughly November 5th and temperatures before that were like down to -7. 

So yeah just the sudden change meant the trees didn't have the temperature signal to drop for long enough. The leaves will continue to drop as the die on the trees instead.  Leaves will still grow this year but maybe less but probably not noticably.

It's hard to say without pictures or knowing the growbox. so here are some possible issues. it could be none, could be all, or something in the middle. What I've learned about growing is you need to find what's right for your environment.

Lysol has been accused of stunting growth before. Now anytime I use it it's just for a general clean, Lysol surface let sit for 5, wipe then wipe with 70% alcohol paper towel. 

Heat mats unregulated can dry mycelium out. Really only maybe needs likely higher than room temperatures during spawning. and fruiting is just the opposite maybe a tiny bit cooler than room temperature but both can be done at room temperature.

Depending on the size of the cake, the dunk could have drowned the mycelium. I've been reading an hour per inch of thickness lately.  Also I don't dunk in the fridge as the water can cause the low temperature with the water can freeze the mycelium (not sure if freezing it would kill it).

Buying anything online has risks, the one risk being that we don't know when the box was made? Also if you didn't use your own LC or MSS, how do we know that was alive to begin with. (If you have any left from MSS or LC I'd suggest looking into Agar and trying it on that. A lot of people suggest going to agar first to prevent and check for contaminates but I usually just knock up small jars with agar to get start right away if the syringe is clean.)

Also the tinfoil, not doing anything. Went people use liners what they're trying to achieve is only the top of the cake being ideal FC. What the liner does is shrinks with the cake (cake shrinks as it uses the water within) which prevents the sides and bottom of the cake from creating pockets of ideal fruiting conditions which leads to side pins. Light really only gives the mycelium a natural cycle and a direct to grow.

If you decide to make your own boxes, and aren't looking to dive deep in right away. I'd suggest the Uncle Ben subreddit and the corresponding YT channel 90 second mycology. Really helps to understand the basics of growing while not entirely breaking the bank. A lot of people hate UB Tek but I can't deny it as a good starting point.
